hook: A phone app can tell you that you walked 3 km today, but not where you ended up. A delivery van can drive 40 km and finish back at the depot. Physics separates how far something went from where it ended up, and that difference decides everything that follows.

prereq.why: Δ is always final minus initial.

chain.effect: it has a displacement, the change in position

chain.cause: The displacement happens over a time interval
chain.effect: its average velocity is Δx divided by Δt

chain.cause: The velocity changes over a time interval
chain.effect: the object has an average acceleration, Δv divided by Δt

ideas: Displacement is a change in position, with a sign for its direction.
Average velocity is Δx/Δt; average acceleration is Δv/Δt.

misconception.right: Acceleration is any change in velocity: speeding up, slowing down or turning.

summary: Displacement is the change in position; average velocity is displacement over time and average acceleration is change in velocity over time, each with a sign for direction.
